subject.title: Bug: Agent outputs ~ tilde shorthand instead of full absolute file paths

question: Should OpenClaw keep home-path shortening as the default in agent-facing and user-visible displays, add an opt-in absolute-path mode, or switch those displays to absolute paths by default?
rationale: Current code and tests preserve shorthand as an intentional display convention, while the issue asks for a different user-visible contract with privacy and compatibility tradeoffs.

options.title: Add opt-in absolute display mode
options.body: Introduce one shared, documented display-policy seam and update the affected helpers/tests so users who need copy-paste absolute paths can enable it without changing defaults for everyone.

options.title: Keep shorthand as the default contract
options.body: Leave the issue open only if maintainers want docs or prompt guidance, or close it later as not planned after explicitly confirming the compact display convention.

options.title: Switch defaults to absolute paths
options.body: Update shared helpers, ACP/session prompts, terminal display, and affected tests to stop home shortening by default, accepting the privacy and UI churn as intended.

recommendation.title: Add opt-in absolute display mode
recommendation.body: Introduce one shared, documented display-policy seam and update the affected helpers/tests so users who need copy-paste absolute paths can enable it without changing defaults for everyone.

likelyOwner.reason: The central helper history points to steipete, and this decision needs ownership of the broad display contract rather than a one-file fix.
